findings.highlight: I find myself gasping for breath.
findings.governingReading: 必死に呼吸を整える is an attempt to steady breathing against sudden nausea, not breathlessness itself.
findings.explanation: Desperately regulating breathing becomes involuntary gasping.

findings.evidenceJa: ね、お兄ちゃん。お兄ちゃんは、わたしのものになったのよね？
findings.governingReading: Illya switches from シロウ to repeated お兄ちゃん when asking him to acknowledge that he belongs to her, then returns to シロウ afterward.
findings.explanation: Illya briefly calls him “big brother” while demanding acknowledgment that he belongs to her. English uses “Shirou,” removing the family address from that coercive question.

findings.highlight: My mouth opens on its own, forming words in quick, shallow breaths.
findings.evidenceJa: 口はひとりでに開き、舌が、浅慮すぎた言葉を繰り返す。
findings.governingReading: 浅慮すぎた言葉 refers to the earlier rash assent; 舌 repeats it against his will. 浅慮 is insufficient thought, not shallow respiration.
findings.explanation: Repeating carelessly chosen words becomes forming words in quick shallow breaths.

findings.highlight: Otherwise, I don't even want to think about what might happen to me.
findings.evidenceJa: そうしなければ取り返しのつかない事になる。
findings.governingReading: 取り返しのつかない事になる marks irreversible harm if he cannot escape, repeated immediately afterward.
findings.explanation: Certainty of irreparable consequences becomes reluctance to imagine the outcome.

findings.governingReading: 用意はできてる asks whether preparations are already complete; Liz replies they are.
findings.explanation: A readiness check becomes a request to prepare the dress.
